Somewhat off-topic, but not really:

I had a co-worker in college, and him and his group of friends would go dumpster-diving on a pretty regular basis. I remember asking him several questions about it, and he had informed me that lots of big stores will throw perfectly good clothing that has gone out of style into their dumpsters, but in order to prevent homeless people from taking it, they will dump bleach all over the discarded products in order to make them worthless. He reasoned that they do not donate unused clothes to people in need, and prevent the people in need from taking them, because people who are willing to buy those clothes at retail price will no longer desire certain brands of clothing if people who are of a lower class are wearing the same brand of clothes that they do. I know this is a little different, but it is very similar in terms of a product's aesthetics increasing its value.

I don't have a source, other than the co-worker I spoke to some years ago. But it sounds pretty believable considering what we already do with food, and it's an interesting thing to think about.
Judging by the size of the average Walmart shopper, I don't we waste food at all. :)

I work with a local homeless shelter, and it's incredible how much waste a single restaurant or market creates. Very few of them are willing to part with this; a 501(c) is a bare minimum, if they're even willing to unlock the dumpsters.

A small pizza place gave us over 70 perfectly edible pizzas from the weekend alone, and I'm not even in an urban area.
